From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Windsor: lead-liaison request & board-sync windows for close plan

Team —

Attached is the latest mutual action plan (WIN_MAP_v3.xlsx) and a compact evaluation runbook (Final_Eval_Steps.docx). Windsor is asking for a board-level alignment (they call it a "board-sync") to sign off on the final evaluation gating and procurement runway.

High-level asks: 
- We need a single Redwood lead-liaison (executive point of contact) for the board-sync. This person will handle the 15-min pre-brief with Windsor execs and lead the 60–90 minute board-sync.
- Confirm two candidate board-sync windows (we'll pick one): May 10–14 week and May 17–21 week. Windsor prefers mornings ET.
- Finalize evaluation gates for the first EB (board-sync) so we can feed the SLA exceptions doc into procurement ahead of time.

Please review the MAP and eval steps and:
1) Voluntarily claim lead-liaison (we're short on bandwidth so a single point is critical).
2) Flag any missing artifacts or required approvals (e.g., SLA exceptions) you need from Legal/Delivery.
3) Confirm availability across those two weeks (morning ET times).

Attachments: WIN_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP), Final_Eval_Steps.docx

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Mid-Market Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Couple of operational thoughts: 
- For gating, we should make the first board-sync a "validation board-sync": focus on evaluation results and procurement terms; reserve the final signature for the second board-sync only if all critical KPIs are green. That reduces risk.
- Priyom — can you scope the run of show (who speaks when, where to place the demo, and the 10-min QA)? I can help with exec slide pack.
- I'm attaching an SLA exceptions template we typically give to procurement (Windsor-SLA-exceptions.pdf). Please review and mark any items Legal must triage.

If Ben is lead-liaison, PM/Delivery should join the pre-brief and the validation board-sync (Hannah please add Matt from Delivery if possible).

Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
